title: ADAS Sensor Calibrations Desk Guidance: Where the Alignment Comeback Window Ends
content:
Where the comeback window on an ADAS Sensor Calibrations customer-pay order ends follows how the order arose:

- for an order opened on the **customer's own request**, it ends on the order's opening date, the day the customer reported the trouble;
- for an order opened on a **network customer-pay repair**, it ends on the date of the order's first alignment check, the day the vehicle already on the network's rack was first measured;
- for an order opened on a **glass replacement**, as for any other customer-pay order, it ends on the date of the order's latest out-of-spec alignment check, the day the misalignment was found.

## Records that fix the end date

| How the order arose (the order's recorded source) | End of the comeback window | Record read |
|---|---|---|
| Customer request | Opening date of the calibration order | The order's opening date |
| Network customer-pay repair | Date of the order's first alignment check | The date of check number 1 on the order |
| Glass replacement, or any other customer-pay source | Date of the order's latest out-of-spec alignment check | The most recent check on the order whose result was out of spec |

## Illustrations (hypothetical calibration orders, each with a first alignment check on 12 May and an out-of-spec check on 20 May)

- Opened on the customer's own request on 10 May: the window ends on 10 May.
- Opened on a network customer-pay repair: the window ends on 12 May.
- Opened on a glass replacement: the window ends on 20 May.
